chunks: And that which was narrated is - Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from al-Haytham ibn 'Urwah al-Tamimi, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram who wishes to perfect his wudu (ablution), and a hair or two hairs fell from his beard, so he said: 'It is nothing (no penalty).'
He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty.

key_terms.إِسْبَاغَ: To perfect or complete (the ritual act)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person in ihram accidentally loses beard hair while washing their face during wudu?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the accidental loss of one or two beard hairs during the completion of wudu does not incur a penalty, emphasizing the principle of ease in ritual obligations. This ruling is grounded in the Quranic verse 'He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty,' which Shia jurists cite to justify leniency in minor, unintentional acts during the state of ihram. The hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between deliberate transgression and natural, minor occurrences when determining kaffarah.
